transcript:
HEADER
Date: 2025-12-08
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CISO - Atlas), Ethan Ross (Head Infra), Kim Alvarez (Security Eng), Liam O'Neal (DevOps)
Shared artifacts: Atlas_pen_test_2025-11-30.pdf (customer link), redwood-security-whitepaper.pdf (Redwood link), KMS-integration-sample.zip (Redwood link)

SUMMARY (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Quick retrospective review of pen test results; focus on high/critical findings, patch cadence and vulnerability windows, secure SDLC tweaks, and clarifying encryption/KMS integration. Action items agreed for annotated report and a KMS technical session.

TRANSCRIPT BODY:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, Atlas team — appreciate you making time. Myself Jordan Kim, AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya Desai, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maya: Good thanks. Busy, as always.
[00:09] Ethan: Hi, yeah thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Jordan: Cool. The goal for today is we wanna walk the pen test findings at a high level, make sure we understand Atlas's remediation priorities and timelines, and then nail down next steps for the KMS and RBAC follow-ups. If that works for everyone?
[00:25] Maya: Yep, that sounds right. We also want to tighten patch windows and confirm any temporary mitigations we can accept while devs work on fixes.
[00:33] Priya: Great. Just to add — we'll also share an annotated PDF with suggested mitigations and a sample KMS integration when we follow up.
[00:40] Kim (Customer): Quick note — some of the pen test text got garbled in the PDF header, so apologies if the report names look weird, the attachment should be the latest.
[00:47] Jordan: No problem. We'll reference the findings by the numeric IDs in the report. Okay, diving in — Finding 001: exposed dev secrets in a public S3 bucket. Atlas, can you give a quick status?
[00:58] Liam: Yeah, that was — that was a leftover from a CI job. We've removed the bucket and rotated the keys, but we haven't completed a root cause blameless postmortem yet.
[01:12] Maya: The keys were rotated and we put a deny on public ACLs, but we want to confirm the vault (we currently use an internal vault) integration with our CI is fully automated; some rotations were manual.
[01:24] Priya: Got it. For automation, we can share a sample workflow that calls your KMS + Vault and rotates CI tokens on a schedule. We have a small sample that uses vault's API and AWS KMS — note: K M S was sometimes transcribed as 'K m s' in earlier notes — ignore that.
[01:41] Ethan: That would be helpful. Also, regarding the vault, are we looking to use Redwood's managed key support or integrate Atlas's own HSM?
[01:52] Jordan: We support both. For Private deployments, customers often prefer to bring their own KMS/HSM. We can map the key material and rotation policies. Priya can go over the specifics.
[02:03] Priya: Sure — quick overview: Redwood's platform can be configured with either external KMS via IAM roles and key aliases, or you can manage keys in a customer-managed KMS. Rotation policies can trigger automated rewraps. We'll send example IAM policies and terraform snippets.
[02:18] Maya: One of our auditors asked specifically about key rotation window and whether Redwood keeps any plaintext logs — we need explicit confirmation in writing.
[02:27] Jordan: Short answer: we do not persist plaintext model inputs or secrets. We can provide the SOC 2/ISO statement and an excerpt from our logging policy. Priya, follow-up?
[02:36] Priya: Yes, we'll attach the SOC 2 control map and a logging excerpt. There are a couple of caveats: audit logs that reference request metadata (IDs, timestamps) are retained for X days by default; we can extend retention for enterprise customers. We'll note retention in the follow-up.
[02:51] Kim: Cool. Next — Finding 004: privilege escalation via a misconfigured role in our staging cluster. That one's high.
[02:59] Ethan: We validated the role and removed the extra permissions, but I'm worried about similar misconfigs elsewhere. We're trying to standardize via IaC templates.
[03:10] Priya: That's a really common pattern. We recommend a least-privilege baseline and RBAC naming conventions. If you can share the role matrix, we can suggest mapping into Redwood's role model (service-level roles vs admin roles).
[03:23] Maya: We will share. Also, what about SSO? We currently use SAML with our IdP. We want to ensure SCIM provisioning is in scope so roles auto-sync.
[03:34] Jordan: We support SAML SSO with optional SCIM for provisioning. We'll need SAML metadata and a list of roles that you want provisioned. Priya, can you outline the SAML/SCIM flow?
[03:44] Priya: Absolutely. The flow is: IdP sends assertion -> Redwood validates signature and maps attributes -> SCIM endpoint is used for group sync. We'll include an example mapping in the follow-up.
[03:55] Liam: Important — audit logs: how long are admin action logs kept? Our compliance team asked for 12 month retention for admin actions.
[04:04] Priya: Default is 90 days in hosted, but Dedicated/Enterprise can extend to 12 months or more with an add-on. We also support log export to your S3 or SIEM — we can set up streaming to your Splunk/Datadog.
[04:17] Maya: Ok that's helpful. Next area — patch cadence. The report flagged slow response on CVE triage for a couple infra packages. Our internal SLA for critical patches is 7 days; we want to align on what 'emergency' looks like when Redwood needs to patch runtime components.
[04:33] Jordan: For hosted runtime components, Redwood's security team operates on a prioritized patch cadence. For critical CVEs affecting runtime, we aim for a 72-hour mitigation window or a documented temporary workaround. For Dedicated or Private deployments where customers manage nodes, we provide CVE alerts and recommended builds.
[04:49] Ethan: For Private, we handle node patching ourselves. We need a clear runbook from Redwood on hotpatch steps so devops can apply them safely.
[04:58] Priya: We'll share a runbook and a 'hotpatch checklist' — includes KV cache migration steps, model compatibility notes, and rollback commands. Note: KV cache sometimes came up as 'K V cache' in some notes — see our best practices doc.
[05:12] Maya: There's also a finding on dependency management in our ML-serving CI. The pen test called out out-of-date Python libs in one container image.
[05:21] Liam: That has a patch target of 2 weeks per our SDLC. We run nightly SBOM scans but the pipeline didn't block build on vulnerable libs.
[05:30] Priya: We recommend integrating SCA tooling (Snyk, or OSS scans) into the CI gate. Additionally, Redwood's Optimize team can provide guidance on combining quantized model builds with SBOM generation so you don't break performance pipelines.
[05:45] Maya: Good. Let's talk mitigations priority — which items should Atlas patch first?
[05:50] Jordan: From Redwood's POV: 1) secrets exposure (Finding 001) — rotate and automate; 2) privilege misconfigs (Finding 004) — apply least privilege and IaC guardrails; 3) dependency vulnerabilities in containers — CI gating; 4) audit log retention and export — configure long-term export for compliance.
[06:10] Kim: On audit logs — one of the pen test notes said logs were accessible to more roles than necessary. Is there a pattern to lock that down?
[06:18] Priya: Yes, make audit logs write-only for most roles; separate read access behind a compliance role. Also implement RBAC for log archives. We'll provide an example ACL.
[06:28] Ethan: Regarding remediation timelines, we need to present to our board on Friday. Can Redwood provide an estimated remediation timeline and effort estimate?
[06:36] Jordan: We can. We'll produce a remediation plan with low/med/high effort estimates for each finding. That will be part of the annotated PDF.
[06:44] Maya: Another question — do you have any guidance on secure SDLC steps for model deployment? We want to ensure our A/B rollout doesn't leak sensitive prompts during canary.
[06:56] Priya: For safe model rollout: use staging with masked inputs, prefix anonymization, and enable prefix KV cache isolation per deployment. Also use canary routing with percentage-based traffic and model-level logging only to ephemeral stores. We'll share the SDLC checklist.
[07:14] Liam: For models, how do you handle data residency? A couple of our customers require EU-only processing.
[07:22] Jordan: Redwood supports region pinning and data residency controls. For hosted, you can pick EU regions; for Private, data never leaves your VPC. We'll provide the region residency statement and a short diagram.
[07:34] Kim: Auditors also asked about attestations for SOC 2 & ISO. Can you send cert copies and control mappings?
[07:41] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll attach certs and the SOC 2 control map to show where Redwood controls map to Atlas requirements.
[07:47] Maya: Ok, shifting back to patch cadence — what about notification channels? We want automated Slack + email alerting for critical CVEs.
[07:56] Priya: We can configure the alerting integration — webhook to your Slack, plus emails to the security alias. For Dedicated customers we can also open a support channel with priority routing.
[08:07] Ethan: On the pen test follow-up: can Redwood comment on mitigations that are acceptable as interim controls vs ones that require code changes? The board will want to know which fixes are quick wins.
[08:18] Jordan: Sure — in the annotated report, we'll label each mitigation as 'temporary workaround' (config change, revoke creds, ACL changes) vs 'code change required' (CI gating, model handling).
[08:28] Maya: Perfect. A few smaller notes: 1) confirm retention window for audit logs in our account, 2) provide list of which logs contain PII and how they're redacted, 3) sample SAML attribute mappings.
[08:41] Priya: We'll include those three in the follow-up. Also, we'll provide an example terraform snippet for KMS keys and a snippet for SCIM group mapping.
[08:52] Liam: For urgency, we have two high findings and three medium. We can target the highs in the next sprint. Low ones can be backlogged.
[08:59] Jordan: Sounds pragmatic. We'll mark the action items with recommended due dates.
[09:03] Maya: Anything else from Redwood?
[09:05] Jordan: One more thing — we recommend running a short tabletop of the incident response for data exposure scenarios; Redwood can co-facilitate if you want.
[09:14] Maya: Yes, let's do that. Book a 90-minute tabletop with our incident response and legal.
[09:20] Jordan: Great, we'll propose times. Okay let's recap the next steps...
[09:25] Priya: I'll take point on the KMS runbook and terraform samples. Jordan will send the annotated pen test PDF and remediation plan. Maya will send the RBAC matrix/SAML metadata.
[09:36] Jordan: Recap and timelines — Jordan: annotated report by 2025-12-12; Maya to send RBAC/SAML by 2025-12-11; Priya KMS runbook by 2025-12-19; schedule tabletop for the week of 2025-12-15.
[09:55] Ethan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:57] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the links.
[10:00] (call ends)

NOTES ON TRANSCRIPTION QUALITY: There are occasional mis-hearings around acronyms (KMS -> K M S), KV cache written as 'K V cache', and some names may be off by a character. Use the meeting metadata for authoritative attendee list.
